decisions.reason: As a core next-generation extension of the firm's airfield lighting control business, it fits the installed base and long airport procurement cycles mean the option should be kept open despite limited short-run market evidence.

The air situation display strengthens the firm's integrated surveillance offer and can be carried at modest incremental cost while demand in airport modernization projects remains uncertain and slow to resolve.
The airport systems training program leverages existing service capabilities, supports customer lock-in around the installed base, and is inexpensive enough to keep as a complementary option.
This narrow training course appears to overlap with the broader training offer, and with little visible evidence of traction its upside is too limited to justify separate resources.

The collaboration software tool is closely aligned with the firm's strategic move toward real-time information sharing and collaborative decision-making, so it is worth retaining as a low-cost growth option.

The multilateration surveillance system is a strategically important, high-value extension of the firm's core airport operations portfolio, so management should keep it while adoption uncertainty continues to resolve.
